subject: Recap & next steps — Migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Holodocs)
messages:

Subject: Recap & next steps — Migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Holodocs)

Hi Lukas / team,

Thanks again for the 30-minute call earlier — wanted to capture a concise recap, confirm the key success criteria you called out, and propose next steps so we’re aligned. TL;DR: you’re exploring moving generation and some safety tooling off OpenAI/Anthropic to an open-model stack to reduce cost, avoid vendor lock-in, and get more control over embeddings/safety.

Pain points you shared
- Runtime costs: OpenAI/Anthropic spend has grown faster than usage; current bill ~ $65k/mo, unpredictable spikes from bulk summarization jobs.
- Latency & burst behavior: peak latency and queueing for live assist workflows; need consistent 95th-percentile latency
- Vendor lock-in: function-calling & safety features differ; rewrites for tool integrations are costly
- Data residency & compliance: some PHI-adjacent data; need to prove isolation and auditability for pilots

Current stack (as described)
- Generation: OpenAI (gpt-4.1-family) for user-facing assistants
- Safety / guardrails: Anthropic checks on a subset of outputs for higher-risk flows
- Embeddings: Pinecone + in-house vector-store adapters
- Orchestration: LangChain thin layer; batch jobs in GCP us-central1

Top-line success criteria (your framing)
- Prompt parity: equivalent instruction-following and hallucination rate reduction vs current baseline on the customer prompts (within a 10% delta on manual evals)
- Embeddings quality: semantic similarity recall/precision on internal benchmark >= current provider or acceptable tradeoffs for cost
- Latency: 95th <= 350ms for the majority of interactive calls (where feasible)
- Cost target: at least 2x reduction in per-token spend on bulk workloads, predictable unit pricing for production
- Implementation effort: minimal changes to app code (prefer an API shim) with safeguards for function/tool calling

Preliminary open-model shortlist (we will validate with your prompts)
- Meta Llama 2 (70B) — candidate for parity on instruction-following
- Mistral / Mixtral variants (dense instruction-tuned) — good for cost/latency tradeoffs
- Mosaic MPT-30B (instruct-tuned) — strong for long-form and controlled outputs
- Falcon / TII 40B — faster inference in some infra configs

Compatibility & risk notes
- Function calling: Anthropic/OpenAI function schemas differ; expect a small adapter layer but need to validate streaming/cancel semantics
- Safety: Anthropic-style guardrails will need either a secondary model pass or integrated classifier; we should include a safety regression test suite in the POC
- Embeddings drift: we’ll compare cosine similarity on a 500-sample benchmark you provide

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Tech deep-dive (1.5h): engineering to engineering session to review sample prompts, current token profile, and top risk flows — propose Wed 2026-07-28 10:00am PT.
2) POC scope: 2-week pilot with 1-2 model candidates (dedicated/dev pool), include these tests: instruction-following, function-calling compatibility, embedding parity, and safety/regression checks.
3) Redwood to deliver: POC test plan, ballpark cost estimate (for dedicated capacity + pilot), and a pilot quote (see attached).
4) Holodocs to deliver: sanitized sample prompt set (<= 2k prompts), a 500-sample embedding evaluation set, and your compliance checklist for data residency.

Attachments included: holodocs_poc_testplan.md (initial draft), holodocs_current_token_stats.csv (token distribution snapshot), redwood-poc-quote.pdf (ballpark).

If that matches your view, I’ll lock in the engineering deep-dive and get Monica / Neha on the invite.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Holodocs)

Karthik,

Thanks for the clear write-up — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Compliance: we’re not fully PHI; it’s PHI-adjacent (clinical notes anonymized) but we must run in a VPC and have KMS integration for keys during pilot.
- Embeddings: yes, Pinecone is the vector store. We also run a nightly batch re-embed of new docs.
- Function calling: our assistants make synchronous tool calls (search, internal DB write, page render) — streaming response behavior is critical for UX.

On the shortlist: we’d prefer to prioritize models with good streaming and tool-call latency characteristics — happy to let you pick two candidates to test.

Wed 7/28 10am PT works for the deep-dive. Please send a calendar invite and an attendee list.

Also: can you include a short note on how Redwood handles safety/regression monitoring during pilots? We need to present that to our security lead.

Best,
Lukas Novak
Head of Product, HoloDocs
lukas@holodocs.com

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — Migration off proprietary LLM APIs (Holodocs)

Lukas — quick engineering note from our side on the POC checklist (attaching a longer test plan):
- Compatibility tests (must-pass): streaming endpoints, function-call schema mapping (we’ll validate calls + args roundtrip), embedding cosine similarity >= 0.92 vs your current embeddings on core queries
- Quality tests (scored): instruction-following on 200 prompt pairs (A/B vs current), hallucination rate (manual eval on 100 outputs), latency percentiles (p50/p95 for 1-token, 64-token response shapes)
- Safety/regression: automated classifiers + manual review on 200 safety-sensitive prompts; we’ll provide a dashboard for regression alerts during pilot
- Ops: KMS integration for pilot keys, VPC peering for data isolation, and centralized audit logs (we’ll provide retention options)

Attachments: holodocs_poc_testplan.md (detailed checklist), holodocs_current_token_stats.csv (uploaded). I’ll also include a sample rubric for manual evals.

I’ll be on the deep-dive; Rishi will join to scope infra and cost assumptions.

—Monica
